scenario: WIBTA for testing my boyfriend? | So a short backstory on me, I am a model. And with that most of my previous relationships stem from the guys I am dating on really dating me because of my looks and the "status symbol" of dating a model not because of me as a person. This is something that has caused a lot of anxiety and depression in my life and I have been really trying to find people in my life that care about me not what I look like. Now that is not to say that my looks can't play a role (physical attraction is important to me as well) but I can't be with anyone where that is the only or main reason why they are dating me. So that brings me to a guy a started dating fairly recently. I really like him and he seems like a good guy. Takes interest in my hobbies and is supportive of what I do. He enjoys lazy days around the house and cooking for me at home instead of always wanting to go out (which with a lot of guys it just seemed like they wanted to show me off). So I really really like him. But his friend DM'd me the other day and told me, "Hey, just thought you should know. You boyfriend has been telling anyone who will listen about all the dirty shit he gets to do with 'this model chick I have been banging'. I'd want to know. Hope for the best!" I have only met this guy once and I don't know how close he is to my boyfriend nor do I know why he told me this. For all I know he is just trying to start drama. The problem is I know how badly I want to believe my boyfriend. And if he were to tell me that it isn't true I would probably believe him. But that thought of "what if" would constantly be in my head from now on. So would I be an asshole if for the next month or so I stop wearing makeup when we go out and I don't put out at all (just come up with whatever excuse I need to when he starts trying to make a move)? If I test what his motives truly are? Part of me feels like this is wrong but the other part knows this is the only way I can fully 100% put this behind me. And if his friend is lying I can commit to him 100%

It’s more likely to create a cycle of suspicion and resentment than to give you the clarity you’re looking for. --- ## Why that feels wrong | What you’re planning | Why it can backfire | |----------------------|---------------------| | **Withholding makeup** | You’re using your appearance as a lever to gauge his reaction. That turns a personal choice (how you present yourself) into a test, which can feel like a betrayal of your own agency. | | **Creating a “test” scenario** | It assumes that the only way to know his motives is to see how he reacts to a fabricated situation. That’s a form of manipulation that can damage the relationship’s foundation of honesty. | | **Relying on a third‑party rumor** | The friend’s message is an unverified claim. Acting on it without confirmation can lead to unnecessary conflict or hurt if the rumor is false. | | **Letting anxiety dictate actions** | The “what if” scenario you’re worried about is a common anxiety pattern. Acting on it can reinforce that pattern rather than breaking it. | ### The bigger picture - **Trust is built on communication, not tests.** If you’re worried about his motives, the healthiest route is to talk to him directly. Ask him about the rumor, how he feels about you, and what he wants from the relationship. - **Your self‑worth isn’t tied to how you look.** You’ve already expressed that you want a partner who values you beyond your appearance. That value is something you can affirm by setting boundaries that respect your autonomy—like deciding when and how you wear makeup—without turning it into a test. - **Manipulation can backfire on you.** If he discovers you’re withholding makeup to test him, he may feel betrayed and defensive, which can push him away rather than bring him closer. - **Anxiety can distort reality.** The “what if” scenario you’re fearing may never happen, but the stress of constantly watching for it can wear you down. A direct conversation can reduce that mental load. --- ## A constructive path forward 1. **Clarify your feelings first.** - Write down what you’re afraid of and why. - Identify what you truly need from the relationship (trust, respect, honesty). 2. **Plan a calm conversation.** - Choose a neutral setting. - Use “I” statements: *“I felt uneasy when I heard the rumor, and I’d like to understand what’s going on.”* - Ask open‑ended questions: *“Can you tell me about what you’ve been saying to others?”* 3. **Set personal boundaries (not tests).** - Decide how you want to present yourself in public and private. - Communicate those boundaries to him: *“I’d like to wear makeup when I go out, but I also want to feel comfortable being myself.”* 4. **Seek external support if needed.** - A therapist or counselor can help you manage anxiety and build healthy communication habits. - A trusted friend (not the one who sent the rumor) can offer perspective. 5. **Give him a chance to respond.** - If he’s honest and apologizes, you can decide whether that restores your trust. - If he’s evasive or defensive, you’ll have concrete evidence to inform your next steps. --- ### Bottom line Testing your boyfriend by withholding makeup is a manipulative tactic that risks damaging the trust you’re trying to protect. A direct, honest conversation—grounded in your own boundaries and self‑worth—is a healthier, more respectful way to address the uncertainty. If you’re still unsure after talking, consider whether the relationship aligns with the values and respect you deserve.
